subject: Audit evidence packaging and temporary BYOK exception — MedTechCo pilot
messages:
From: Sara Alvarez <sara.alvarez@medtechco.com>

Cc: ComplianceOps <compliance-ops@medtechco.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Audit evidence packaging + BYOK exception request (pilot)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited about Redwood's latency numbers. We're starting a short pilot for a set of telemetry endpoints and have two asks to unblock our procurement/compliance review: 

1) Evidence packaging: can you provide an evidence bundle that contains exported audit logs for the pilot window (1 week), plus a manifest that maps log files to customer IDs? We prefer CSV manifest + MD5 checksums.

2) Temporary BYOK exception: our security team would like to run the pilot with our KMS keys (we understand full BYOK + on-boarding is longer). Would Redwood consider a temporary, timeboxed BYOK exception for the pilot (30 days) with scoped access and audit controls?

I've attached a brief scope doc and a sample manifest template. If you can point us to the right internal folks, we'll start formal evidence requests.

Attachments: MedTech_Audit_Scope_v1.pdf; Sample_Audit_Manifest.csv

Best,
Sara Alvarez
Head of Compliance Programs
MedTechCo

Neha/Marcus — can you confirm what evidence artifacts we can reasonably produce in a 7–10 day turnaround and whether a 30-day temporary BYOK model is feasible without full onboarding?

I'll capture action items here once we align.

Thanks for the ping, Dylan — Sara, hello. Quick security triage below after an initial read of the scope doc. I added numbered questions to make this actionable.

1) Retention & scope: you asked for a 1-week export. Confirm: do you need raw per-request payloads or just platform-level audit logs (access, API invocation, token scoping)? Raw payloads are sensitive and trigger additional controls.

2) Manifest requirements: CSV + MD5 is fine. We need to confirm the set of identifiers to include (customer_id, project_id, request_id, timestamp, checksum). Will MedTechCo accept hashed user identifiers (SHA256) instead of plaintext PII? That reduces scope.

3) BYOK model: for a temporary 30-day exception we need answers to:
   - How will keys be provided? (EKM/HSM endpoint vs key material upload)
   - Who will hold rotation rights during exception?
   - What are the exact scope and allowed operations for the keys? We will not allow key export or unmanaged key storage in our environment.

4) Audit of actions: if we permit a temporary BYOK flow, we require additional logging (KMS key usage logs) and a signed exception form that lists TTL and rollback procedures.

Proposed immediate deliverables (7–10 business days):
- A sample exported audit bundle (platform access logs + manifest) for a sanitized resource set (no raw payloads).
- A BYOK temporary exception checklist and a draft exception form for signatures.

I can author the exception form template if you want — Marcus/Marcus-infosec, please confirm operational feasibility and whether we need infra changes to capture KMS usage events at the granularity Sara needs.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Audit evidence packaging + BYOK exception request (pilot)

Thanks — quick infra/product read and a proposed plan.

What we can deliver in 7 business days (engineered, testable):
- One-off audit export containing API access logs, auth events, routing records and per-request metadata (no raw customer payloads). We'll generate CSVs and a manifest with SHA256 checksums (MD5 available on request).
- A compact manifest schema (we'll attach a sample CSV) that maps request_id -> timestamp -> resource_id -> hashed_user_id -> checksum. This should meet your procurement needs.

BYOK temporary path (operational model):
- Option A (preferred): MedTechCo provides an EKM endpoint (cloud KMS or HSM) that we call for crypto ops. No key material comes into Redwood. This is the lowest-risk and supports a 30-day pilot immediately.
- Option B: customer-supplied key material is uploaded into a customer-isolated envelope. This requires legal and infra controls; turnaround is longer (3–4 weeks).

Constraints and mitigations:
- We will capture KMS call logs and include them in the audit export. We cannot allow key export.
- If Option A is chosen, we can enable a scoped service account and restrict calls to the pilot resources.
- We need an approved exception form for Option B (if chosen).

Action items I propose now:
1) Sara: confirm whether MedTechCo can stand up an EKM endpoint for the pilot (Option A).
2) Neha: we'll work with you on the exception template and KMS usage capture.
3) Dylan: once we get answers, I'll schedule a short runbook review with operations.

Attachments: Sample_Audit_Manifest.csv

--
Marcus Lin
Principal Product Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — this thread is in good shape. Short legal/programs notes and next steps for closing the pilot exception.

- BYOK temporary exception: Legal needs a signed exception form that includes (a) TTL (we suggest 30 days), (b) exact scope of key usage, (c) incident contact and rollback playbook, (d) confirmation that no key export will be permitted. I have a draft DocuSign ready; Sara, if you authorize, I'll send the DocuSign to your approver. (see link below).
- Evidence delivery: acceptance criteria should be included on the procurement side (format, checksum algorithm, PII policy). If MedTechCo accepts hashed identifiers and no raw payloads, we can proceed under standard data-handling controls.
- Escalation: if MedTechCo requires payload-level exports or long-term BYOK, we will need a formal private deployment/contract (Redwood Private) — we should avoid this for the pilot.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: Sara confirms EKM/Option A availability and signature approver.
- +1–7 business days: Redwood provides a sanitized sample export and the exception form.
- +7–10 business days: pilot evidence export (if pilot runs immediately).

I will prepare the DocuSign with TTL=30 days and the exception checklist and copy legal on the envelope. Marcus/Neha, please flag anything that must be in the form text.
